title: API Development
excerpt: APIs and integrations that move data between your product and the tools around it, with errors you can see.

seo.title: API Development | Mohit Walia
seo.description: APIs and integrations that move data between your product and the tools around it, with errors you can see.

hero.heading: APIs and integrations with a contract you can read.
hero.subtitle: REST endpoints, webhooks, and third-party connections. Stripe, CRMs, and internal tools included when they are part of the job.

overview: I build the boundary between systems: the endpoints your app calls, the webhooks other tools call, and the mapping between their data and yours.
problem: Integrations start as a script. Then a field changes, a webhook is missed, and the only record of what happened is a log nobody can search.
solution: Each connection has a written shape, retries where they help, and a stored result so you can see what was sent and what came back.

features.title: A readable contract
features.detail: The inputs and outputs are documented next to the code.

features.title: Webhooks you can replay
features.detail: A failed delivery can be inspected and sent again.

features.title: Third-party care
features.detail: Stripe, CRMs, and similar tools are connected with their failure states in mind.

process.title: Discovery
process.detail: We pin down the outcome, the constraints, and what the first release has to do.

process.title: Planning
process.detail: I turn that into a scope, a sequence, and the technical approach.

process.title: Development
process.detail: I build in small slices you can review, on the stack this service uses.

process.title: Testing
process.detail: We check the flows that matter before anything is treated as finished.

process.title: Launch
process.detail: I ship it, watch the first days, and leave you with a clear way to change it.

benefits.title: Failures are data
benefits.detail: You can see the payload, not just a red light.

benefits.title: The product stays in charge
benefits.detail: External tools do not become the only copy of your data.

timeline.detail: The data, the auth, and the failure cases.
A run against the real service in a safe mode, then production.

faqs.question: Do you design public APIs for other companies to call?
faqs.answer: Yes. Auth, versioning, and a short reference are part of that work.

faqs.question: Can you connect a tool we already use?
faqs.answer: If it has an API or webhooks, usually yes. I will say so after looking at their docs, before the build starts.
